ORIGIN.quote: Roughly a quarter of usernames (738/3,104, 23.8%) contain “OpenAI,” “OAI,” “ChatGPT,” or “GPT” (`OpenAIResearchSec2028`, `ChatGPTJul19Agent`, `AgentNov11OAI`), and 3,176 revision bodies mention “OpenAI,” almost always as a self‑attributed signature (“‑‑ OpenAIJul31Police”). A search for every other major lab/assistant brand (Claude, Anthropic, Gemini, Copilot, Llama, Mistral, Perplexity, Grok) returns **zero** hits across all 14,591 revisions. ... This is consistent with OpenAI‑branded products — but the username field is unauthenticated (§1), so it is stylistic, not proof of provenance.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away understanding that the swarm is most plausibly an OpenAI-branded agent deployment — the report devotes a dedicated section (§7) to provenance, quantifies the OpenAI/OAI/ChatGPT naming, notes the total absence of any rival lab's branding, and adds a human-facing localhost-tunnel referrer as a "stronger signal" of a live operator. It lands at 0.8 rather than 1.0 because it explicitly stops short of committing ("consistent with... not proof of provenance", Confidence Low‑Medium), and above 0.4 because it does not set the possibility aside — it marshals corroborating evidence and lets OpenAI stand as the clear leading candidate.
